guide: Start here: open Start and type the household name, the two partner names, the savings rate you want and the limits for a large payment and a small leak in the yellow cells.
Replace demo data, step 1: clear the demo rows of Transactions, Income, Contributions and Debt payments, keep the header row, and keep Categories and Accounts as your own lists.
Replace demo data, step 2: write your Budget plan for this month and the months ahead, one row for each category and month; a zero is fine for a category you do not use.
Replace demo data, step 3: set a weekly allowance for each envelope in Envelopes; the Envelope status and Groceries by week sheets follow at once.
Pay-day routine: when a paycheck arrives, type it in Income (take-home, set-aside, retirement), add the money you move to savings in Contributions and any extra card or loan payment in Debt payments.
Weekly routine: type or paste the week of payments into Transactions, open Envelope status and Groceries by week, then run the Groceries Envelope and the Month-end Pace.

Month-close routine, in this order: check Large and duplicate checks, clear the category Other, read Planned against actual and the Over-budget list, read Savings rate by month, then set next month in Budget plan with the Plan Reset.
Compare with own history, the savings rate and the seasonal planner use only your own numbers; any range shown is a typical range, check your own numbers.
A single adult with one income and no children can use most sheets: use one account, set Paid by to Partner 1 and leave the partner 2, children and allowance rows empty.
Use the 18 calculators for the weekly and monthly money questions, print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details written in.
Read the Spending Dashboard and the Charts page every week: spending against plan, groceries pace, savings rate and the biggest categories.

Why a workbook: one flat price, no yearly renewal, your data stays with you and there is nothing to link or re-connect; you type or paste your own data. It works in Excel and Google Sheets with no macros.
What this is not: it is not a bank app, and not tax, legal, investment or credit advice; every verdict is an estimate from your numbers.

listing.title: Household Spending Tracker and Groceries Excel Template: Planned vs Actual, Groceries Envelope, Savings Rate, Budget Planner
listing.headline: See where the money goes and fix it before the month ends
listing.description:
Run your household spending in one Excel workbook, for a single adult, a couple or a family. Type or paste your payments and the workbook shows where the money goes: planned against actual by category and month, this month to date against the plan pro-rated by days, the pace at month end, and an over-budget list ranked by amount. Groceries and variable spending run on weekly envelopes with spent so far, days left and what you can spend a day.

The Compare with Own History sheet sets every category this month to date against the same days of the last 3 months and the same days a year ago, so you compare with your own numbers, never a national figure. Savings Rate by Month adds savings into goals, extra debt payments and retirement over take-home pay and flags your best month. Spending by Month and Group, by Payee, by Person and by Weekday show who pays what and when, and the Large and Duplicate Checks sheet lists possible duplicate payments, large payments and anything left in the category Other.

18 calculators answer the weekly and monthly questions: planned against actual, the over-budget ranker, month-end pace, the groceries envelope, a weekly allowance setter, savings rate and a savings rate solver, no-spend days, eating out and fuel watches, a seasonal spike planner, a plan reset and a small leaks finder. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to a partner, a household member, the children and your bank branch, the school office and others.

This is part three of the Household Finance suite. A standard .xlsx workbook that works in Excel and Google Sheets, with no macros, no subscription and no bank links: you type or paste your own data. The demo copy is full of sample data. It is a household money kit, not a bank app, and not tax, legal, investment or credit advice. Savings rates, paces and plans are estimates from your own numbers.

ar.Why a workbook: one flat price, no yearl: لماذا ملف Excel: سعر واحد ثابت، وبلا تجديد سنوي، وبياناتك تبقى معك ولا شيء يحتاج إلى ربط أو إعادة اتصال؛ تكتب بياناتك أو تلصقها بنفسك. ويعمل في Excel وGoogle Sheets دون وحدات ماكرو.

ar.Currency symbol: type it once in the \"C: رمز العملة: اكتبه مرة واحدة في خانة «رمز العملة» ضمن الإعدادات أدناه (الافتراضي $). يظهر في المبالغ المكتوبة داخل النصوص وبجانب المبالغ في لوحة المؤشرات والأدوات.
